with the same one-key policy the gateway behaves as before; with a list policy the first admission is
refused MODEL_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED until the owner's reconcile command adopts the list

choosingTheKey: inside reserve(), after the budget row is locked FOR UPDATE (the one serialization point) and after every
existing refusal, the ledger reads the open marks and takes the first hash of the pinned list that has
none; the reservation row is inserted with that credential_hash in the same transaction
the gateway passes the row's credential_hash to the adapter, which holds one SarvamAdapter per key and
sends with exactly that one; a hash it does not hold is an unknown outcome, never another key
no round-robin and no per-call choice: the choice depends only on the list order and the open marks

theCallThatReceivesUsedUp.choice: it fails with a retryable code; it is not sent again inside the same reservation
what: only for a list policy and only for the two cited answers (429 insufficient_quota_error, 403
invalid_api_key_error) with a readable body: in one transaction the key gets its mark and the call is
closed as settled at 0 micro-INR with a receipt (HTTP status, response hash) and its error kind
the caller gets 503 MODEL_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED or MODEL_CREDENTIAL_INVALID (today's codes) with
details.retryable true while another key remains; the mapping teacher turns both into a manual plan
the next admitted call, or the caller's second attempt of the same invocation, goes to the next key
asking again with the same invocation and attempt returns the same refusal, never an output
why: one HTTP request stays one ledger row with one key and one receipt: nothing is folded into another row
a second send inside the same reservation would put two requests inside one pace interval, could chain
through all keys within one 45 s deadline, and after a crash between the two sends would leave a
dispatched row whose first answer is lost; the two-attempt rule would also stop meaning two requests
closing at 0 is the only existing state that ends a dispatched row (released requires no dispatch, and
changing a CHECK is not additive); left open, MODEL_EXPOSURE_PENDING would stop every later call
theCallThatReceivesUsedUp.assumption: a refused request is not billed; the documentation is silent, the first live refusal checks it

everythingElseInAList: rate limit: the shared cool-down and the held reservation of today; no other key is tried
timeout, network failure, 5xx, unreadable body, missing usage: held as today; nothing moves
any other 4xx: held as today; capability_denied, 402 and 401 still block the pool as today
caps, single in-flight call, reservation before dispatch, two attempts and pace: the same queries, over
all rows of all keys; a zero-settled refusal counts as a call of the person's daily call cap
reconciliation: the budget row's credential_hash becomes, for a list, the hash of the ordered list of key hashes; for one
key it stays hash(key). config_hash already covers the names and their order.
so adding, removing, reordering or replacing a key changes one of the two and the existing check refuses
with MODEL_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED; an unchanged list never does
demo-gateway.mjs reconcile --reason <text> (owner, demo stopped) adopts the configured policy when it
differs from the pinned one only in its key names or key values, and no call has open exposure; a
change of any cap, price, bound, pace or label is still refused, as today
marks follow the key's hash, so a used-up key stays used up wherever the new list puts it
